<details markdown="1">
<summary>Parameter provenance</summary>

- **Origin of the parameterization:** Solomatova (2016), Table 7 and MINUTI analysis: coupled HS/LS reference branches inferred from measured compression trajectories, including the cited experimental datasets. Model decomposition does not make these ab-initio fits.
- **Equation:** Table 7 and MINUTI discussion: third-order Birch-Murnaghan high-spin and low-spin reference branches in a coupled spin-crossover fit.
- **V0:** Table 7 HS column: 75.55 A^3 per conventional B1 cell.
- **K0:** Table 7 HS column: 159 GPa.
- **K0 prime:** Table 7 high-spin K0' column.
- **Original dataset:** Solomatova et al. refit the P-V data of Marquardt et al. (2009b), DOI 10.1016/j.epsl.2009.08.017.
- **Fit relationship:** The paired branches, transition pressure, and transition width form one source spin-crossover model; Peritheos currently stores only the independently executable reference branches.

</details>

- **V0:** Section 3.1.1 and Table 2: 75.62 +/- 0.06 A^3 from ambient single-crystal XRD, used as the reference-volume anchor, not an unconstrained P-V regression coefficient.
- **K0:** Section 3.1.1: KT0 = 158.2 +/- 2 GPa; room-pressure Brillouin results constrain this isothermal modulus.
- **K0 prime:** Section 3.1.1: KT0 prime = 3.98 +/- 0.14.
- **Uncertainties:** Printed errors retained. Table 2 specifies one-sigma volume errors; confidence for fitted modulus errors and covariance is not stated.
- **Temperature:** Room-temperature measurements; catalog reference uses 300 K.
- **Fit selection:** Table 2 source\_order 1-14 (P &lt; 45 GPa); ambient row anchors V0. The complete 29-row resource also preserves 9 mixed-spin and 6 LS observations.
- **Brillouin constraint:** Section 3.2 separately reports Brillouin-only adiabatic KS0 = 161.4 +/- 1.1 GPa and KS0 prime = 3.98 +/- 0.14. These are not KT0 or additional P-V rows. The precise weighting of the ambient constraint is unavailable. EPSL Table S2 separately reports ambient KS = 165 +/- 3 GPa; the 161.4 GPa fitted intercept is not this ambient observation. The supplement still does not specify the exact constraint implementation.

</details>

<details markdown="1">
<summary>Parameter provenance</summary>

- **Origin of the parameterization:** Marquardt (2009), Section 3.1.2, Table 2 and Table S1: XRD/Brillouin constraints and experimental LS sensitivity fits. Assumed V0/K0\_prime alternatives are fit constraints, not theoretical observations.
- **Equation:** Section 3.1.2: third-order Birch-Murnaghan isothermal EOS; Table S1 publishes the constrained LS fit family.
- **V0:** Table S1 row 12: 72.59 A^3 per conventional B1 cell, fixed from the stated LS/HS ratio 0.96. Preserve printed V0 rather than recomputing from the rounded ratio.
- **K0:** Table S1 row 12: KT0 = 199 GPa fitted to LS XRD observations. No statistical uncertainty is printed.
- **K0 prime:** Table S1 row 12: KT0 prime fixed at 3.5.
- **Fit selection:** Table 2 source\_order 24-29, P &gt; 63 GPa; six LS observations. Mixed-spin rows are excluded.
- **Derived checkpoints:** Table S1 KT columns at 69, 70.1, 75.8 and 81.2 GPa are derived LS model outputs, not additional observations. Columns at 45.9, 52 and 59 GPa include the mixed-spin population response and must not be compared with the pure-LS BM3 derivative.
- **Summary rows:** min, max and avg summarize the ensemble by column; they are not three additional source fits. The average of nonlinear model curves is not generally the curve of the averaged coefficients.

</details>
